---
title: "Coherence of pairwise threshold decisions"
subtitle: "3.10 · after Kline, Rose and Walters (2024), §V.E"
description: "Pairwise threshold decisions can conflict with each other, even when no strict cycle occurs."
---

A pairwise threshold reports a direction when its error probability is strictly below $\tau$. Applied separately
to each pair, this rule can produce directions that no grade report can reproduce. For example, if the report
withholds A–B and B–C, A and C must share a grade too. A stated direction for A–C would contradict those two
decisions. The triple display counts these contradictions and directed cycles. The card overlay shows which
directions the archived grade report states under the same released probabilities.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Race λ .25.** Naive thresholding states 1,575 directions. Among 147,440 triples, 32,773 have two pairs
  withheld and the third stated. For the selected triple, the withheld
  pairs would force every firm into the same grade, contradicting the stated direction.
- **Race λ .10.** The two-withheld count is 24,278. The triple selector and map arrows locate other conflicts in the matrix.
- **Race λ .50.** The count falls to 15,107. The rule reports more directions, yet fewer triples have two withheld pairs and one stated pair.
- **Race λ .75.** The count falls again to 3,108. Even without a strict directed cycle, the withheld pairs can conflict with a direction the rule states.
- **Race λ .25, card blocks.** The card withholds 575 confident pairs and states 324 directions whose errors
  exceed τ. The selected triple retains its identity within these blocks. KRW's card has no cap on the number of grades,
  so these differences arise from coherence.
- **Gender λ 1.00.** All 4,656 pairs are stated, but 1 directed cycle precludes a coherent grade report. The absence of cycles
  at the race baseline does not extend to every target and threshold.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
A shared grade leaves the direction between two firms unranked. We count threshold decisions using the released
probabilities for the signed target. KRW selected the archived cards with their own code and archived
probabilities. Here we evaluate those cards under the released probabilities and use the overlay to compare
their directions with the separate pairwise decisions.
